data.title: LongPoint Announces Cash Distribution on Moat ETF
data.description:
Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 20, 2026) - LongPoint Asset Management Inc. ("LongPoint") is pleased to announce the monthly cash distribution for the Moat Active Premium Yield ETF (the "Moat ETF") listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange under the symbol (MOAT: TSX). The Moat ETF seeks to provide high income and moderate capital growth primarily by writing put options on a portfolio of North American equity securities.

Unitholders of record on November 27, 2026, will receive a cash distribution payable on December 2, 2026.

Details of the per unit distribution amount are as follows:

Moat Active Premium Yield ETF

Distribution per Unit: $0.22

Cusip: 606953107

ISIN: CA6069531078

Payment Frequency: Monthly

The Moat ETF is doing what it is meant to do. This will be the eleventh monthly distribution since inception. This will now bring total distributions to $2.28 since January 14th, 2026. In the portfolio manager's opinion, this distribution yield is supported by the diversification of the ETF's portfolio alongside the potential downside room between current stock prices and put option strikes sold.

Distributions for the Moat ETF will vary from distribution period to distribution period. For further information regarding the Moat ETF, please visit www.longpointetfs.com/etfs/moat.

About LongPoint Asset Management Inc.LongPoint Asset Management Inc. is a Canadian owned and operated company which delivers innovative ETF solutions designed to enhance your Canadian investing journey. Our dedicated team leverages deep industry connections and local insights to design, build, and launch exceptional ETFs tailored for Canadian investors. LongPoint also offers its unique ETF Partnership Platform, which simplifies the launch, operation, and growth of ETFs for its partner asset managers. LongPoint was Canada's fastest growing ETF provider in 2025, on a percentage basis, and offers 54 Canadian-listed ETFs with approximately $440 million in assets under management. Discover the advantage of investing with LongPoint.

About Moat Financial LimitedMoat Financial was founded in 2023 by Chris Thom after fifteen years at a respected Vancouver based firm. The goal at Moat Financial is to put clients first, provide independent advice and use a variety of investment tools to deliver quality service. Moat's investment philosophy is based on the principles of value investing. Chris is a regular contributor on the BNN segment called "Know Your Options".

data.title: Nasdaq Plunges 5% — WSJ
data.description:
By Jack Pitcher

The tech selloff is getting ugly heading into the close-with AI-related stocks taking another leg lower after Reuters reported that the Securities and Exchange Commission is examining Nvidia's accounting practices.

The Nasdaq composite recently touched fresh lows, down 5.1%. The index is down more than 1,000 points currently, a dubious distinction hit just three times previously, according to Dow Jones Market Data.

The Nasdaq-100, meanwhile, is flirting with a bear market, trading close to 20% below its recent peak.

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).

data.title: Grain Futures Finish Mixed to End Shaky Week for Commodities — Daily Grain Highlights
data.description:
By Anthony Harrup

  • Corn for March delivery fell 0.8% Friday on the Chicago Board of Trade to $4.48 3/4 a bushel, closing out a negative week for commodities with losses.
  • Wheat for March delivery declined 0.5% to $5.92 a bushel.
  • Soybeans for January delivery rose 1.1% to $12.20 3/4 a bushel.

HIGHLIGHTS

No Risk Premium: Grains trading is likely to remain choppy in the short term as markets tussle with currency issues, South American weather and changes in global trade flows with no Russia-Ukraine peace deal likely, AgResource said in a note. "ARC maintains there's little to no risk premium in grains markets currently, and the assumption is that geopolitics and South American weather progress smoothly through the balance of 2026," the firm said. They also added that it won't take much in the way of shifting grain flows or weather scares in South America to give prices a boost.

Forecast Tweak: The International Grains Council raised its 2026/27 global production estimate for wheat and coarse grains by 1 million metric tons to 2.428 billion tons, with higher wheat and barley numbers offsetting lower corn. The biggest changes were increases for Turkey, Australia and Argentina, and a reduction for the U.S., the IGC says. Ending grain stocks are raised by 7 million tons to 626 million tons, "inflated by unusually heavy inventories in Russia and Ukraine." Soybean production is seen at 439 million tons, unchanged from the October forecast.

Flash Sale: The USDA reported sales of 100,000 metric tons of soybean cake and meal for delivery to Spain during the 2026/2027 marketing year.

INSIGHT

Bears vs. Bulls: Corn futures typically rise between Thanksgiving and year-end, with the March contract making an average gain of 32 cents a bushel between Nov. 20 and Dec. 31 in the past 12 years, Naomi Blohm of Total Farm Marketing said in a note.

"The old expression for grains: 'the bears get Thanksgiving, but the bulls get Christmas' may have rung true with the lower price action this November," she said. While each year has its own fundamental supply and demand perspectives, the March contract has had some sort of rally during the period since 2014. Some lasted only days, but others stretched to weeks.

Looking Up: Citi Research maintains a positive view on a number of agricultural commodities including corn and soybeans, and sees the recent drawdown as a buying opportunity. "We still expect El Niño to have larger impact on yields in the next 3-6 months," global head of commodities research Max Layton said in a note. Markets will also start taking notice of the Black Sea closure as Ukraine typically ramps up exports during this time of year. "Exports of both corn and soy have been relatively strong and we expect China delivering on their commitments on buying U.S. soy and potentially corn," Layton added.

AHEAD

  • The USDA will release its weekly Grain Export Inspections report at 11 a.m. ET Monday.
  • The USDA will release its weekly Crop Progress report at 4 p.m. ET Monday.
  • The USDA will release its monthly Cold Storage report at 3 p.m. ET Tuesday .
  • The EIA will release its Weekly Petroleum Status Update report at 10:30 a.m. Wednesday

Write to Anthony Harrup at anthony.harrup@wsj.com

data.title: Gold's slide deepens as AI rout, rate-hike bets hurt bullion
data.description:
Key points:
  • Gold slips for fifth session, hits lowest since September 2025
  • Markets may soon see gold and silver prices bottom — analyst
  • Gold, silver, platinum, palladium head for second straight weekly decline

By Anjana Anil and Vishak Mathew

Gold's bearish spell continued on Friday as it floundered to a 14-month low and headed for its worst week in eight months, amid pressure from a hawkish interest rate outlook and an AI-linked stocks selloff.

Spot gold fell 3% to $3,514.08 per ounce by 3:25 p.m. ET (2025 GMT), after touching its lowest level since September 2025 at $3,502.49 earlier in the session.

Bullion has shed about 9.4% so far this week, the most since the week ended March 20.

US gold futures for December delivery settled 4.6% lower at $3,515.40 per ounce.

"The ongoing AI-related equity selloff is prompting some forced liquidations of gold positions to cover losses," said David Meger, director of metals trading at High Ridge Futures.

Stock markets stumbled around the world on Friday after Anthropic's IPO failed to restore investors' faith in the AI trade, with US futures dropping and Asian shares heading for their worst week since 2020.

"Higher interest rates, stronger dollar, the prospects for ongoing high inflation, which prompts the Fed to continue to raise interest rates — all of those factors that we have been seeing — negatively affect gold," Meger said.

Gold's fall has been accentuated by comments from US Federal Reserve policymakers that echoed hawkish tones in the Federal Open Market Committee's (FOMC) October meeting. Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson flagged inflation risks that could warrant another interest-rate increase, reinforcing expectations that US borrowing costs will rise further.

Markets see a 96% chance of a 25-basis-point US rate hike in December, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

"Prices in the next few sessions could still drop a lot more. But from a time perspective, it's very likely that we're going to see a bottom in the gold and silver markets sooner rather than later," said Jim Wyckoff, a market analyst at American Gold Exchange.

Spot silver fell 4.1% to $40.99 per ounce, 66.3% below its record high of $121.64 hit in January.

Platinum dropped 3.4% to $1,296.50, and palladium slid 2.1% to $890.19. All precious metals are poised for their second consecutive weekly declines.

data.title: ICE Review: Canola Fails to Shake Up-Down Pattern
data.description:
WINNIPEG, Manitoba--Intercontinental Exchange canola futures were lower on Friday, maintaining the teeter-totter pattern of trading this week.

A trader said canola need more export interest to swing higher.

The trader added that's aided by weaker Canadian dollar.

Loonie The Canadian dollar fell back on Friday afternoon, with the loonie at 69.78 U.S. cents, compared to Thursday's close of 69.85.

Mixed comparables Crude oil turned around to climb higher, with spillover going into the vegetable oils. Chicago soybeans and soymeal finished the day on the plus side, while the soyoil along with European rapeseed and Malaysian palm pulled back.

Exports, domestic use While the Canadian Grain Commission said canola exports were down on the week ended Nov. 15, the year-to-date tally of 2.66 million tonnes was nearly 830,000 tonnes better than a year ago.

Domestic use improved on the week, with the cumulative total climbing to 3.73 million tonnes, up 260,000 tonnes from the same time last year.

Canola revised Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada trimmed 100,000 tonnes from its call on canola ending stocks for 2026-27 at 1.87 million tonnes.

In 2025-26, the carryover was 1.89 million tonnes.

AAFC kept its canola export forecast at 7.7 million tonnes and boosted domestic use by 1.41 million tonnes at 14.5 million.

Statistics Canada is set to issue its updated production report on Dec. 4. StatCan's September report pegged the canola crop at 22.05 million tonnes.

Prices There were 56,767 canola contracts traded on Friday, compared to 63,520 on Thursday. Spreading accounted for 32,658 contracts traded.

data.title: Robusta coffee hits 3-year low as Vietnam harvest ramps up
data.description:
Robusta coffee futures on the ICE exchange hit three-year lows on Friday, posting a 10% weekly loss, as the harvest in top grower Vietnam ramps up.

Raw sugar fell again, after a sharp drop on Thursday, and hit a three-month low.

COFFEE

* Robusta coffee settled down $97, or 3.3%, at $2,881 a metric ton, after setting a three-year low of $2,854.

* A Vietnam-based dealer noted that ICE futures have fallen sharply yet local price discounts for physical robusta are still easing. "That is the clearest sign so far of growing supply pressure," he said.

* Elsewhere, the recent weakness of Brazil's real currency has encouraged exports from the world's second largest robusta producer.

* Brazil's currency fell to its lowest level since April 2025 on Thursday.

* Arabica coffee fell 2.7% to $2.685 per lb. The market lost 1.8% in the week.

SUGAR

* Raw sugar ​settled down 0.13 cent, or 0.8%, at 17.03 cents per lb after setting a three-month low of 16.82. The market posted a 7.5% weekly loss.

* Funds have been scaling back a net long position in raw sugar ahead of the year end, with the market looking technically bearish after breaking below key support levels.

* Physical sugar broker Deepcore noted some bearish fundamental factors also, namely, estimates of 13% growth in top grower Brazil's 2027 sugar output and limited interest in India's duty-free raw sugar import programme.

* Citi, however, said that uncertainty about the supply outlook in India and the recent selloff due to weaker Brazil currency could be a buying opportunity.

* White sugar was little changed at $487.90 a ton.

COCOA

* London cocoa ​​​settled up 58 pounds, or 1.4%, to 4,094 pounds per ton. It gained 1% weekly.

* Low port arrivals in top grower Ivory Coast are helping underpin cocoa, as are estimate for sharply reduced 2026/27 output in Ecuador.

* Ample availability of cocoa from the 2025/26 crop, however, continued to keep a lid on prices.

* New York cocoa gained 1.3% to $5,270 a ton. It was flat for the week.

data.title: Nvidia's accounting is a focus of US SEC investigation, sources say
data.description:
By Chris Prentice and Alexandra Alper

The US Securities and Exchange Commission is probing Nvidia's accounting practices, said two people briefed on the matter, adding to the legal woes facing the scandal-hit chip giant.

The Wall Street Journal on Tuesday reported that the SEC was probing Nvidia but said it could not ascertain the focus of the investigation. The people, who spoke to Reuters on condition of anonymity to discuss confidential issues, said SEC enforcement staff are scrutinizing potential accounting issues at the company.

A spokesperson for the SEC declined to comment. Spokespeople for Nvidia did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Prices of Nvidia shares extended losses and were down about 13% on Friday, according to LSEG data, after Reuters reported details of the SEC probe. They had been down more than 6% before Reuters published its report.

Reuters could not immediately determine when the SEC opened its inquiry or exactly what potential accounting issues the watchdog is examining. Investigations are not evidence of wrongdoing and many close without resulting in enforcement action.

Still, the accounting focus of the probe, which Reuters is reporting for the first time, increases pressure on Nvidia, whose investors are still reeling from revelations about ousted CEO Jensen Huang's extramarital relationships, including with Alice Huang, who US authorities suspect is a Chinese spy. China has denied she is a spy.

Alice Huang led Singapore-based Megaspeed, historically a large Nvidia chip customer, people familiar with the matter have said. US authorities have been investigating Megaspeed since 2024 over possible violations of export controls related to alleged shipments of Nvidia AI chips to China, the US Justice and Commerce departments said this week.

The crisis has sent shares in Nvidia, a linchpin of the AI boom, tumbling more than a third and stoked calls in Washington for tougher action on tech threats posed by Beijing.

Megaspeed has said Alice Huang left the company in August 2025 and that it conducted "lawful business." Reuters has not been able to reach Alice Huang. Jensen Huang admitted to an affair in a November 8 statement following the reports of his relationship with Alice Huang, without referring to her by name.

The SEC probe is the latest of Nvidia's legal woes. The Justice Department has also been reviewing Nvidia's $12.9-billion deal to buy open-source platform Hugging Face alongside a broader antitrust investigation into the company's acquisitions and practices, Reuters reported last month.

SINGAPORE ACCOUNTING CHANGE BACK IN FOCUS

Last year, Nvidia changed how it reports geographic revenue, using customer headquarters rather than billing addresses, which it said would better reflect the geographic profile of its revenue. The change resulted in Singapore being removed from its geographical breakdown.

The Financial Times, citing company accounts, reported on Tuesday that Nvidia had made the change even as Singapore sales soared to almost half its global revenue.

That accounting shift has drawn renewed press scrutiny in the wake of the Alice Huang scandal.

Southeast Asia has become a hub for chip smuggling to China since the Biden administration barred advanced AI chip exports to that country over concerns they could boost Beijing’s military.

Analysts and investors have also grown increasingly concerned about circular AI financing deals, in which chipmakers including Nvidia have pursued complex financial arrangements to help customers fund purchases of their chips and the construction of costly AI infrastructure, such as data centers. Nvidia has backed AI companies and cloud providers and provided guarantees connected to data-center projects that use its equipment.

Critics say such arrangements can make it harder for investors to assess the quality of chipmakers' revenue and their true financial exposure. Speaking to Reuters last month, SEC enforcement chief David Woodcock said the agency was examining AI companies' corporate disclosures to ensure issuers are giving investors the full picture on potential risks.

On its Tuesday earnings call, Nvidia's interim CEO and former CFO Colette Kress said the company was proud of its role in supporting the AI industry, but would be far more selective moving forward about AI industry financing deals.

The SEC under President Donald Trump has pulled back on enforcement, saying it will focus on bread-and-butter securities fraud, including accounting violations that have long been a mainstay of its enforcement work. It recently launched a new financial reporting and accounting unit within its enforcement division, aimed at developing cases in accounting and auditing areas.

data.title: Take-Two's 'Grand Theft Auto VI' Hits Nearly $4 Billion in Sales on Launch Day
data.description:
By Ben Fritz

"Grand Theft Auto VI," the latest installment of the Take-Two Interactive Software video-game series, grossed nearly $4 billion in sales by the end of its launch day, according to the company.

Take-Two said "GTA VI" sold 32.5 million pre-ordered games to customers who wanted to download and play as soon as it was available Thursday. The retail value of the sales through the end of launch day were about $3.79 billion, which Take-Two said was a record for any entertainment property.

When "Grand Theft Auto V"--the previous edition of the series published by Take-Two-unit Rockstar Games--launched in 2013, it sold $800 million worth of copies on its first day. That game cost a minimum of $60, while the basic version of "GTA VI" costs $80.

Shares of Take-Two are down slightly, at $208.55, amid a broader market selloff late Friday, after rising to $218.69 earlier in the session.

data.title: Trump Continues To Insist On Huang’s Return At Nvidia’s Helm, Threatens US Firms Building Overseas Data Centers
data.description:
Key points:
  • Trump advocated for a second chance for former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang following a scandal involving a suspected Chinese spy.
  • Nvidia would reinstate Jensen as CEO “if they were smart,” Trump said during a White House press conference.
  • Trump also threatened heavy taxes on American companies expanding AI data center capacity outside the United States.

President Donald Trump on Friday urged Jensen Huang to apologise and return to lead Nvidia Corp.(NVDA), even as the board of directors explicitly signaled no plans to reinstate the former chief executive.

Speaking during a White House press briefing, Trump praised Huang's past impact on the company and argued that he deserves another opportunity. Trump noted that he still favors Apple Inc. CEO Tim Cook as his preferred successor to Huang, while adding that he would like to see Huang get a second chance.

Trump called Huang one of the world’s sharpest minds and credited him with giving the U.S. a decade-long lead over rival companies. He said he would like to see Huang offer a “big apology” and step back into the role. He also added that Nvidia’s board should reinstate Jensen as CEO, “if they were smart.”

“I’d like to see Jensen make a big apology and go back,” Trump said Friday at a White House press conference. “He put us in a position where we are literally 10 years advanced over other companies.”

Trump Discusses Nvidia And Chip Exports 

According to Trump, Huang’s status came up during his meeting earlier in the week with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, where Trump said Xi likewise described Huang as brilliant. Those high-level talks unfolded against the backdrop of disclosures that Huang had a relationship with an alleged Chinese spy tied to a Singapore-based firm that acquired advanced Nvidia chips.

The controversy also exposed visible divisions inside the U.S. government over its China policy Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has publicly faulted the Commerce Department, headed by Secretary Howard Lutnick, for failing to stop advanced chips from reaching China.

Meanwhile, during the same press conference, Trump lauded Lutnick’s role at the center of a scandal involving AI chips smuggled to China.

“I have not lost confidence,” Trump said in response to a question about whether he had lost faith in Lutnick.

Tax Threats On American Firms

Separately on Friday, Trump warned that the U.S. government plans to slap steep taxes on American companies constructing data centers in foreign countries. The legal basis or the degree of taxation to be levied was not discussed.

Trump said U.S. businesses are free to build abroad but cautioned that they would face a massive tax, emphasizing his preference for projects to be built within the U.S.

Although the United States holds the largest concentration of computing power globally, firms are also expanding into regions such as China, parts of Europe and Latin America and India.

Major technology companies, including Microsoft Corp. (MSFT), Alphabet Inc. (GOOG, GOOGL), and Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN), have committed hundreds of billions of dollars to expand computing capacity.

Trump singled out Google over data center investments in Finland rather than directing all of that spending to the U.S., even as the company has simultaneously backed major domestic projects.

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits was ‘bearish’ on the SPDR S&P 500 ETF and the SPDR Dow Jones ETF (DIA), while was ‘bullish’ on the tech-heavy Invesco QQQ (QQQ) ETF that tracks the Nasdaq 100.
